comment: A State of East Asia levies a value added tax of its own, and the common
system of VAT of Directive 2006/112/EC does not reach it: what this table
says of it is what it says of Japan and Korea. China levies 增值税 under
the Value-Added Tax Law of the People's Republic of China, adopted on
25 December 2024 and in force since 1 January 2026, whose article 10 sets
the rates at 13 %, 9 % and 6 %, and zero on exports.
territories.name: China
territories.legal_reference: Directive 2006/112/EC, article 5(2): the common system of VAT applies in the territory of the Community as defined by the Treaties, and a State outside it is a third country for every rule the Directive carries. China levies a value added tax of its own under the Value-Added Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (中华人民共和国增值税法, in force since 1 January 2026), whose article 10 sets the rates at 13 %, 9 % and 6 %, and zero on exports.
